articles.title: T&E Development Buys West Chelsea Site for $34M From PPHE Hotel Group
articles.narrative: T&E Development has acquired a 9,875-square-foot development site in West Chelsea, Manhattan, from PPHE Hotel Group for $33.5 million. The vacant lot, previously slated for a hotel and luxury condominiums, offers 74,063 square feet of development potential under current zoning and is now expected to be redeveloped into a residential project. The seller cited significant changes in New York's regulatory landscape for hotel development as a reason for divesting the property, while the buyer is poised to deliver new residential units into a market segment currently underserved by new construction.

data_points.address: 538-542 West 29th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Vacant lot with C6-3 zoning within the Special West Chelsea District, not requiring an affordable housing component.
data_points.project_notes: The 9,875-square-foot vacant lot was previously acquired in March 2019 for approximately $42 million by a joint venture between PPHE Hotel Group and Largo, with plans for a 98-key hotel and 55 condos. Demolition permits were filed in late 2023.

articles.market_intelligence: West Chelsea is experiencing a shortage of new condo construction, with only one building currently under construction between West 20th and West 30th streets. Nearby condo developments have achieved average sales of approximately $2,884 per square foot, and Chelsea pricing has increased by 44 percent since 2020, marking the largest five-year increase among all Manhattan submarkets. The market for buyers in the $2,000 to $2,700 per square foot range is currently underserved.

articles.title: L.A. County Investment Sales Jump 28% in July Thanks to Multifamily
articles.narrative: Commercial real estate investment sales in Los Angeles County saw a significant acceleration in July, with a 28.5% jump in dollar volume compared to the previous year, reaching $2.1 billion across 7.25 million square feet. Multifamily properties were the primary driver, accounting for 58% of all investment with $1.22 billion in sales, reflecting a 55% increase year-over-year. Retail also experienced substantial gains, while industrial sales volume increased but dollar volume remained flat, and the office sector was the only major property type to decline in both sales volume and square footage.
articles.market_intelligence: Los Angeles County commercial real estate investment sales in July saw a 28.5% increase in dollar volume year-over-year, reaching $2.1 billion. Multifamily sales volume increased 55% year-over-year, with average pricing up 28.7% to $376/SF. Retail dollar volume rose 40% from a year ago. Industrial dollar volume remained flat despite a 71% increase in square footage traded, with average pricing falling 3.6% to $273/SF. Office sales volume and square footage declined 9.7% and 23.4% respectively from July 2025, with average pricing dropping 23.5% to $250/SF.

articles.title: New York City’s Technology Labor Market Has Surpassed San Francisco: Report
articles.narrative: New York City has surpassed the San Francisco Bay Area in total tech employment for the first time, according to a CBRE report. New York's tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025, an 8.4% increase from 2022, while San Francisco's tech employment declined by 6% to 375,730 jobs over the same period. This shift is attributed to New York's diversified job market, with a significant portion of its tech workers employed in finance, insurance, and real estate, providing resilience against tech industry downturns. The city also benefits from a strong university system and comparatively lower wages, making it attractive for tech companies seeking East Coast headquarters. This growth is reflected in Manhattan's office market, where tech and AI companies are actively leasing significant space.

articles.market_intelligence: AI leasing activity in Manhattan's office market has already surpassed 1.8 million square feet year-to-date in 2026, exceeding the total 1.4 million square feet for all of 2025. In San Francisco, AI-related companies have accounted for 30% of office demand since 2023 and half of all lease deals in the first half of 2026.

Principal Financial Group provided the debt for the fully occupied, supermarket-anchored property. The center was originally developed by Mattone Investors six years ago and has maintained strong occupancy, reflecting continued lender interest in well-maintained, grocery-anchored retail assets.

articles.title: Data Center Development Has Domestic Materials Manufacturers Working Overtime
articles.narrative: A new report from Skanska indicates that while overall U.S. development saw uneven progress in the first half of 2026, specific sectors like data centers, power infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and pharmaceutical production are experiencing significant growth. This surge is largely due to investors prioritizing projects with the highest returns amidst rising material costs and ongoing tariff policies. The strong demand in these sectors is causing unprecedented pressure on mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and steel supply chains, leading to increased lead times and higher prices for domestic materials.

articles.title: Core Spaces Breaks Ground on 2,201-Bed Student Housing Project Near Texas A&M University
articles.narrative: Core Spaces has commenced construction on Hub College Station, a substantial student housing development near Texas A&M University. The project will feature two seven-story buildings offering 2,201 beds across 570 units, with completion anticipated for the 2028-2029 academic year. Amenities will include a rooftop pool, a 14,000-square-foot wellness center, and various study and social spaces. Pacific Life provided the construction financing for this significant development.

articles.title: Dwight Capital Provides Two HUD-Insured Loans Totaling $95.5M for Refinancing of Corpus Christi Apartments
articles.narrative: Dwight Capital has provided two HUD-insured loans totaling $95.5 million for the refinancing of two garden-style apartment complexes in Corpus Christi, Texas. The loans, originated through HUD's 223(f) program, will be used by Azali Homes to retire existing debt, fund property enhancements, cover closing costs, and establish replacement reserve accounts for future capital improvements. The properties, La Joya by Azali and Azali Heights, offer a combined 648 units with various amenities.

data_points.property_name: La Joya by Azali / Azali Heights
data_points.notable_features: Both properties offer one-, two- and three-bedroom units with private patios and balconies, and amenities such as pools, business centers, fitness centers, dog parks and playgrounds.

articles.title: Pullman Gateway mixed-use development reaches full occupancy in Chicago’s Pullman neighborhood
articles.narrative: The Pullman Gateway mixed-use development in Chicago's Pullman neighborhood has reached full occupancy, marking a significant milestone in the area's economic revitalization. The eight-acre project, developed by Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives and Hope Center Foundation, features four national restaurant brands and offices for the Chicago Transit Authority's Red Line Extension. This completion coincides with the announcement of the new Pullman Park Retail Center, which will bring additional dining options to the community, further expanding amenities and job creation in the rapidly growing commercial district.

articles.title: RMK Management tackling leasing, property management duties for Chicago’s The Bellwether multifamily community
articles.narrative: RMK Management Corp. has been appointed to manage and lease The Bellwether, a 117-unit multifamily community in Chicago's Loop neighborhood. This 14-story property, an office-to-residential conversion of a historic building at 79 W. Monroe, is already 57% leased with initial move-ins anticipated in late August/early September. The project is notable as the first office-to-residential conversion completed under Chicago's LaSalle Street revitalization initiative, which aims to transform the corridor with mixed-income residential projects.

data_points.notable_features: Office-to-residential conversion; features remote workspaces, fitness center, saunas, dog spa, and a rooftop deck with lounge seating and an outdoor fitness area. Includes 41 Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) units.
data_points.project_notes: Originally built in 1905, with a major expansion in 1924. It is the first office-to-residential conversion completed as part of the city of Chicago’s LaSalle Street revitalization initiative, which includes private funding and Tax Increment Financing (TIF) assistance.

articles.title: Inflation Is Down. But Consumers Aren’t Out of the Woods Yet
articles.narrative: A recent report from Marcus & Millichap indicates that while inflation is showing signs of moderation, consumers continue to face economic headwinds. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) and core CPI both saw slight month-over-month decreases in July, aligning with market expectations and potentially easing pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. However, housing costs, particularly Owners' Equivalent Rent (OER) and apartment rents, remain significant contributors to inflation, and real average hourly earnings declined, suggesting ongoing pressure on consumer purchasing power. Additionally, rising food prices, mixed retail fundamentals, and a softening leisure and hospitality sector point to continued challenges for household budgets, despite a resilient consumer environment where spending remains selective.

articles.title: Retail Regains Its Footing as Demand Returns and Supply Stays Soft
articles.narrative: The retail sector experienced a rebound in the second quarter of 2026, driven by renewed tenant demand and consistently low new construction. This dynamic is creating a favorable environment for landlords and investors, despite consumers becoming more selective. Investment sales volume for retail properties increased significantly in the first half of the year, leading to pricing pressure and cap-rate compression. The outlook suggests continued limited supply and modest rent growth, particularly benefiting discount and off-price retailers.
articles.market_intelligence: Retail demand reversed Q1 negative absorption in Q2 2026. New retail supply remains limited due to higher construction costs and financing challenges, with most new projects being build-to-suit or grocery-anchored developments. Sunbelt markets account for the majority of new construction. Limited supply is supporting modest rent growth nationwide. Stronger sales momentum in H1 2026 is contributing to cap-rate compression. Retail construction is expected to remain sluggish into 2027, keeping vacancies low.

The company, a tenant since 2023, will continue to occupy a full floor that includes a private outdoor terrace and collaborative workspace. The building's premier Midtown location, transit access, and modern amenities were cited as key factors in the decision to renew, supporting the firm's growth and talent attraction efforts.

articles.title: Data Centers Push Into Frontier Markets
articles.narrative: JLL's Midyear North America Data Center Report highlights a significant shift in data center development towards 'frontier markets' due to power constraints in established hubs. Developers are exploring alternative power solutions like co-located generation, on-site battery storage, and microgrids, alongside direct utility partnerships, to overcome long interconnection timelines. This push into secondary regions, which account for 77% of capacity under construction, is driven by greater power availability, builder-friendly regulatory environments, ample land, and lower operating costs. While these developments promise substantial economic benefits for local communities, the industry faces increasing public opposition, necessitating greater transparency and community engagement to address concerns and communicate the advantages of local data center projects.

articles.market_intelligence: Grid limitations in Columbus, OH, are pushing users to secondary markets with available capacity, specifically Van Wert, Lima, and Canton. Southern Virginia and the I-95 corridor are attracting data center projects from nearby Loudoun and Prince William counties due to grid constraints.

articles.title: Investors Anchor Big Capital Into Marinas, Betting On Shallow Supply
articles.narrative: Institutional investors are increasingly allocating significant capital to marina real estate, driven by the sector's attractive fundamentals and limited supply. This trend is leading to substantial mergers and acquisitions, fundamentally reshaping the market landscape through 2027.

articles.title: Developers Eyeing Dallas' 50-Mile Trails Loop For Uptown-Like Opportunities

The extensive trail network is expected to drive demand for residential and commercial projects, creating a new wave of walkable, amenity-rich environments.

articles.title: Developers Line Up To Convert Boston Offices To Housing, But Most Still Stuck At Starting Gate
articles.narrative: Despite a strong push to convert underperforming office buildings into residential housing in Boston, most proposed projects are stalled due to escalating construction costs and complex policy challenges. Developers are finding it difficult to secure financing and navigate regulatory frameworks, hindering the progress of these adaptive reuse initiatives. This situation reflects a broader market trend where the economic viability of such conversions is being tested by current financial and logistical headwinds.

articles.title: Oncology Company Expands Footprint At Hines' Life Sciences Campus
